key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
engineering_relevance: Linking spectral features to lattice-instability symmetry, coupling and dynamics can guide interpretation of perovskite behavior relevant to ferroelectric and photovoltaic materials.
method: Simulate infrared and Raman spectra using machine-learning-based molecular dynamics.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites with polar, tilt-driven or mixed instabilities.
Relate low-frequency features to polarization or dielectric-susceptibility coupling and instability dynamics.
evidence_signal: Simulations across seven compositions show that slow polar reorientations shift dielectric response to very low frequencies, while overdamped tilting modes produce persistent Raman central peaks.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative experimental validation or model-accuracy metrics, limiting assessment of predictive reliability.
paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
